title.narrative: Mitigate the worst effects of water scarcity and hunger in Sub-Saharan Africa

description.narrative: The intervention in Dzaleka refugee camp and the reception areas targets 56,359 individuals, 55% are male, 45% are females.Approx. 3% of the population in Dzaleka are people with disabilites.The cyclone Freddy response in Blantyre targets 13,022 individuals, 35% are male, 65% are female. 10,4% of the population of Malawi are people with disabilities.

The project has three distinct components:(1) Emergency intervention to mitigate the effects of Tropical Cyclone Freddy (TCF) in 5 neighborhoods of Blantyre. This component will be be implemented together with a partner organization (Waste Advisers) and will be finalized by the end of 2023.(2) WASH in Dzaleka Refugee Camp in Dzaleka, and the Refugee Transit Areas in the north of Malawi (Karonga and Chitipa). WASH activities are complemented by an advocacy component on refugee rights implemented by a national partner organization.(3) Advocacy on refugee rights will be implemented by a partner organization, Youth and Society and is linked to component 2.This component will last throughout the entire project span until the end of 2024.
To improve access to safe drinking water and sanitation and providing immediate emergency assistance in periodic humanitarian crises in seven countries in Sub-Saharan Africa.
